h1:
Isan Food in Kamphaeng Phet
Som Tam, Grilled Chicken & Larb
intro: Kamphaeng Phet is the kind of town where punchy Isan food is everywhere — from tiny roadside som tam stalls to long open-air spots out on the bypass where you can order a whole table's worth. We picked the places locals actually eat at and that reviews keep mentioning: 9 spots, with the dishes worth ordering and where each one sits.

blocks.html: Ask anyone in Kamphaeng Phet what to eat for dinner and the answer is almost always som tam and grilled chicken. It's easy to order, easy to share across the whole table, and the shops are spread out both in town and along the bypass road. Some are small mortar-and-pestle stalls that have been around long enough for the neighborhood to know them by heart; others are comfortable spots that stay open late. We've rounded up both kinds.

blocks.text: Isan spots locals in Kamphaeng Phet actually go to

blocks.html: The order below leans on which names come up most often and which are easiest to find — it's not a hard ranking of which one is tastier, since how punchy or mild you like it is personal. Use the area and signature dishes as your guide, then pick whichever is closest to your hotel or on the route you're already driving.

items.name: Som Tam Ko Phai
items.blurb: A som tam shop with a long menu that townsfolk bring up a lot. The grilled chicken is the dish plenty of people order again. Recently renovated, comfortable and roomy — a good pick if you're coming with a group and want to share the whole table.

items.name: Suea Rong Hai
items.blurb: A punchy Thai-Isan spot right on the bypass road in Sa Kaeo subdistrict, with a wider menu than your usual som tam shop. You'll find full-flavored salted-crab som tam, duck larb, dry crispy fried chicken, and a hot-and-sour tom saap. Great for groups who want to order a bit of everything.
items.meta: Sa Kaeo subdistrict · on the bypass road

items.name: Tam Loei Na Kamphaeng
items.blurb: A som tam shop with lots of unusual variations to try — corn som tam, salted egg yolk som tam, seafood som tam. The one they're known for is tam dong daeng, made by pounding fresh khanom jeen rice noodles, with a sharp flavor that's all their own. Grilled chicken wings and sun-dried pork on the side.
items.meta: 94/44 Moo 6, Sa Kaeo subdistrict · delivery on LINE MAN

items.name: Tam Raet Saep Nua By Jao Tok Taek
items.blurb: A som tam shop reviews single out for deep, bold, rounded flavor and good service — a match for anyone who likes their tam heavy and full-on. There's a handful of Isan snacks to order alongside.

items.name: Larb Koi Soi Ju By Makoto Isan Classic
items.blurb: The real deal for larb and koi. If you're a duo who's into proper Isan-style raw meat, this place is on the mark — larb, koi and soi ju, eaten with sticky rice and fresh veg.

items.name: Khrua Isan
items.blurb: An in-town Isan spot that's easy to sit at and easy to reach — good for an ordinary meal when you just want som tam and grilled chicken without driving far. You can order Isan dishes to spec.

items.name: Pho Phet Mae Or (Jaew Hon)
items.blurb: A jaew hon and mu jum spot that also does pork larb, beef larb, tom saap and a thick tom yum. Good for a dinner where you want something warm by the pot with friends.
items.meta: 53 Moo 13, Nikhom Thung Pho Thale subdistrict
items.price: Jaew hon set from ฿150 · larb ฿60–90

items.name: Som Tam Kamphaeng Taek
items.blurb: A som tam shop with an easy-to-remember name that people in town know. Good for a quick meal — order tam and grilled chicken to take away too. Friendly prices.

items.name: Kai Yang Phi Paew
items.blurb: A spot reviews praise for its grilled chicken and som tam in town. Good if you want the grilled chicken to be the star rather than the tam — easy to grab and bring back to your room.

blocks.title: How to order so it's worth it
blocks.html: With three or more people, order 1–2 plates of som tam, half a grilled chicken, plus one larb or tom saap, then add sticky rice per person — you'll get the full range without overloading the table. If you're not great with heat, tell the shop 'phrik noi' (less chili) when you order, because the Isan places here pound a fairly heavy hand.

blocks.html: If it's your first time in Kamphaeng Phet and you're not sure where to start, these are the Isan dishes most shops do well and that rarely let you down.

items: Som tam with pla ra — the shop's litmus test. If the fermented fish sauce is rounded and savory without a fishy edge, the kitchen knows what it's doing.
Grilled chicken — order half a bird to share; the meat should be juicy, the skin fragrant from the fire, eaten with a sour-spicy jaew dip.
Larb & koi — if you're into raw meat, try koi or soi ju at a dedicated larb shop; otherwise cooked pork or duck larb does the job.
Tom saap — pork ribs or soft cartilage in a clear, sour-spicy broth that cuts through the richness when you're eating grilled chicken.
Sun-dried pork / fried chicken — the snacks the kids at the table usually go for; order them for anyone who can't take the heat.

blocks.text: Where to find the most shops

items.name: In town (around Thesa–Cha Kangrao roads)
items.blurb: Small Isan shops that are easy to sit at — grab a quick meal or take it back to your room. Handy if you're staying in town and don't want to drive far.

items.name: Bypass road, Sa Kaeo subdistrict
items.blurb: The zone of long open-air spots that stay open late, with plenty of room and easy parking. Good for coming as a group and ordering several dishes.

items.name: Evening markets / day markets
items.blurb: Almost every market has a som tam mortar and grilled chicken to take away, at easy prices — good for grabbing dinner to eat back at your room.

faq.q: Which Isan restaurant in Kamphaeng Phet is good?
faq.a: The ones locals bring up most often are Som Tam Ko Phai and Suea Rong Hai, both with wide menus covering som tam, grilled chicken, larb and tom saap. For raw-meat larb and koi, Larb Koi Soi Ju By Makoto is more on the mark. Just pick by whichever area is closest to your hotel.

faq.q: Where should I go for larb, koi and raw meat?
faq.a: Larb Koi Soi Ju By Makoto Isan Classic, on Cha Kangrao Road in town, mainly does larb and koi and suits anyone who likes proper, traditional Isan. If you prefer it cooked, you can order pork or duck larb at any of the general Isan shops.

faq.q: How much does som tam in Kamphaeng Phet cost?
faq.a: Som tam runs about ฿40–70 a plate, half a grilled chicken around ฿80–160, and larb or tom saap ฿60–150 a plate. For 3–4 people ordering a full table, expect roughly ฿300–500.

faq.q: Is Isan food in Kamphaeng Phet very spicy?
faq.a: Most shops pound a fairly heavy hand. If you're not great with heat, tell them 'phrik noi' (less chili) when you order, and add snacks like fried chicken or sun-dried pork to the table just in case.

faq.q: Do Isan shops in Kamphaeng Phet open late?
faq.a: The long open-air spots on the bypass road in Sa Kaeo subdistrict often stay open late into the evening, good for a relaxed dinner. The som tam mortars in the markets tend to close earlier, so heading out early evening is the safer bet.
